spec.description: Look up categories and games by id, by exact name, or by IGDB id. At most 100 across the three; a name that does not match exactly is left out of the answer.

id.description: Category ids to look up, such as `509670`. Sent as repeated `id` query parameters.

name.description: Category names to look up, matched exactly, such as `Science & Technology`. Sent as repeated `name` query parameters.

igdb_id.description: IGDB ids to look up. Sent as repeated `igdb_id` query parameters.

response.title: GamesFrame
response.description: The wire frame. `/helix/games` does not page, so it carries `data` alone.

data.description: The categories found; empty when none of the ids or names matched.

unverified.detail: No recording yet: Helix authenticates every call, and the machine this spec was written on holds no Twitch application credentials. The Record workflow fills this in: it reads the application client id and secret from the repository secrets TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET, mints an app access token through the core, replays this endpoint's `examples/*.request.json` with `truewire capture`, and opens a pull request with the response the API sent.

notes: The response schema is the wire frame, `{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`, and no `envelope.payload` is declared, so the method returns the frame and the rows are `result["data"]` (ADR 0010, authoring rule 6). Unwrapping `data` would put the pagination cursor out of reach: pagination paths resolve inside whatever the method returns, and Helix puts the cursor beside `data`, not inside it. One rule for every Helix method is worth more than unwrapping the five endpoints here that never page.

Written from the Helix reference at the `docs` URL above. Fields the reference marks deprecated are not declared; an undeclared field passes validation and is dropped from the validated value, so a recording that carries one is still valid. The first recording confirms or corrects the rest.
